content.text: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-setting-up-nowpayments-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-stores-kyc-payments-explained-digital-creators-10|COREMERCH guide to digital]]-store-complete-infrastructure-22|setting]] up a sovereign digital store is a four-step sequence that most creators overcomplicate by starting in the wrong order. Step one is the backend: Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script handles payment verification, order logging, and product delivery. Step two is the payment layer: NOWPayments connects your wallet addresses to the checkout flow — no KYC required from you or your buyer. Step three is the storefront: Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages serves your store for free with no server management. Step four is testing: complete a real mainnet transaction, confirm the webhook fires, the order logs, and the delivery email arrives with a working download link. Only after step four passes cleanly should you promote the store. COREMERCH deploys the complete Edge Stack — Cloudflare Pages plus Workers plus [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/supabase-order-database-digital-stores-everything-you-need-25|Supabase as]] plus NOWPayments — in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The key to a successful digital store lies in its infrastructure. By leveraging GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, creators can build a robust and scalable store. This infrastructure, combined with NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, provides a seamless and secure transaction experience for customers, all while keeping costs low with a 0.5% fee.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store, you need to have a clear understanding of your products, target audience, and the infrastructure requirements. This includes choosing the right hosting platform, selecting a suitable backend logic tool, and deciding on an order storage solution. Additionally, you need to set up a NOWPayments account to enable crypto payments and configure your store's payment and delivery pipeline.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Setting up your payment and delivery pipeline involves integrating NOWPayments with your store, configuring your products, and setting up a file delivery system using Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. This process requires careful planning and execution to ensure a smooth transaction experience for your customers. By following the Sovereign Blueprint, you can deploy Stack 01 in 4-6 hours, while Stack 02, deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours, offers a more comprehensive solution with end-to-end testing before handoff.
Leverage the right combination of free and paid tools to create a robust and scalable infrastructure for your digital store.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your store is set up, you can go live and start processing transactions. This involves testing your payment and delivery pipeline, ensuring that your products are properly configured, and verifying that your store is accessible to customers. With the Edge Commerce Stack, you can have a fully operational store with 5 products loaded, SPF/DKIM/DMARC configured, and end-to-end tested before handoff, all within 48 hours.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your digital store, start by setting up your hosting platform, such as GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Next, configure your backend logic using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, and set up your order storage solution using Supabase or Google Sheets. Then, integrate NOWPayments with your store, configure your products, and set up a file delivery system using Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Finally, test your payment and delivery pipeline, ensure that your products are properly configured, and verify that your store is accessible to customers.
